title: Book One · Chapter 123: Mrs Lan’s Line
story:
On the third afternoon, a man leaves a large bag in front of Mr Qiu's table. He wants to buy paper. He puts the bag down to count his money.

Mrs Lan opens her door. She cannot pass.

“Whose bag?” she asks.

The man lifts one hand. “Only a moment.”

Mrs Lan waits. He finishes counting. Then he wants to know the price of an envelope. His bag stays in front of her door.

Ronan stands on the other side of the table. He can see Mrs Lan's shoes. They are pointed towards the street.

“You can leave it by my chair,” he tells the man.

Mr Qiu moves the chair and helps the man lift the bag. Mrs Lan goes out without another word.

Ronan thinks the trouble is over. At closing time Mrs Lan comes back with vegetables. She sets them down in her room, then asks Mr Qiu to sit with her.

“The three days are up,” she says.

Ronan stops beside the side door. He is holding an empty pencil box.

“I know,” Mr Qiu says.

Mrs Lan looks at the path through the gate.

“I agreed to a clear way through.”

“The bag was moved.”

“After I asked.”

Ronan wants to tell her about the sales. Mr Qiu sold pencils and a marked book. But Mrs Lan is talking about her path. She could not get through. He puts the box down and goes to Mum.

“Can she make him leave?” he asks.

Mum is sewing a new edge on a shirt. She stops with the needle in the cloth.

“It is her home.”

“It is our way through too.”

“Yes. So we all need a clear way through.”

Outside, Mr Qiu speaks again. Ronan cannot hear every word. He hears “chair” and “bags” and then a long silence.

Mum goes on sewing. Ronan sits beside her. He does not enjoy waiting. He looks at the black cat on the wall. No one has asked the cat to move. It seems happy to stay there all afternoon.

At last Mrs Lan calls him.

“Bring the string.”

They put a line on the ground again. This time Mrs Lan asks Mr Qiu to stand at the table. She carries her vegetable bag through. He moves his chair before she reaches him.

“Customers wait outside,” he says. “Bags stay outside too. I tell them first.”

“And I do not want a large crowd.”

Mr Qiu looks at his small stack of books.

“That would be a new problem.”

Mrs Lan almost smiles.

They agree to another week. At the end of it they will talk again. Can the table stay for longer? How much should Mr Qiu pay to use the space? They can decide the longer time and payment later.

Ronan goes back for the empty pencil box. He puts it on the high shelf with Mum's help. Then he moves his own school bag from the path.

Mrs Lan sees him do it.

“Thank you,” she says.

Ronan smiles at her. He moved his bag before she asked. Now she can pass easily.

Later a neighbour comes to ask about the new table. Mr Qiu walks out to meet her before she enters the gate. He shows her a notebook from the street side. Mrs Lan passes behind him with an empty bowl. No one stops her. Ronan sees her look down at the clear ground, then go on to the tap. This time she can reach the tap easily.

---

重点表达：count＝数；path＝通道；at the end of＝在……结束时。

情节提示：needle＝缝衣针；customer＝顾客；pay＝付钱。

理解：1. Mrs Lan 真正在意的是什么？2. Mr Qiu 为继续摆摊提出哪些做法？
